claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 are recurrent fusions identified in human spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma.
source: We characterize two recurrent fusions, VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2, recently identified in human spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: The abstract directly states these fusions were recently identified in scRMS, and cites prior literature in the introduction (Alaggio et al., 2016; Tan et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2020; Cyrta et al., 2021; Whittle et al., 2022).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins are potent activators of TEAD-dependent transcription.
source: We demonstrate that in contrast to VGLL2 and TEAD1 the fusion proteins are potent activators of TEAD-dependent transcription
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 1B and C) and RNA-seq analysis showing upregulation of TEAD target genes (Figure 1D and E).

claim: The function of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins does not require YAP/TAZ.
source: the function of these fusion proteins does not require YAP/TAZ.
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays showing lack of interaction with YAP/TAZ (Figure 2A-C) and maintained transcriptional activity in YAP/TAZ knockdown cells (Figure 2H).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins recruit histone acetyltransferase EP300 to control TEAD-mediated transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes.
source: we identify that VGLL2 and TEAD1 fusions engage specific epigenetic regulation by recruiting histone acetyltransferase EP300 to control TEAD-mediated transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes.
evidence: Demonstrated by BioID proteomics (Figure 4A), co-IP assays (Figure 4B), and CUT&RUN sequencing showing EP300 occupancy at TEAD target genes (Figure 4C-E).

claim: Small-molecule EP300 inhibition can suppress fusion protein-induced oncogenic transformation in vitro.
source: We show that small-molecule EP300 inhibition can suppress fusion protein-induced oncogenic transformation both in vitro and in vivo in mouse models.
evidence: Demonstrated by A485 treatment reducing target gene expression (Figure 5B-D) and colony formation (Figure 5E-G) in C2C12 cells.

claim: Small-molecule EP300 inhibition can suppress fusion protein-induced oncogenic transformation in vivo in mouse models.
source: We show that small-molecule EP300 inhibition can suppress fusion protein-induced oncogenic transformation both in vitro and in vivo in mouse models.
evidence: Demonstrated by A485 treatment significantly blocking tumor growth in C2C12 allograft models (Figure 6C and D).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 significantly induce transcriptional activation of TBS-Luc reporter in HEK293T cells.
source: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T cells, we found that, in comparison to the VGLL2, TEAD1, and NCOA2 proteins, the VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins could significantly induce the transcriptional activation of the TBS-Luc reporter
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C with statistical significance (****p<0.0001).

claim: The transcriptional activity of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 is comparable to activated forms of YAP and TAZ (YAP5SA and TAZ4SA).
source: their activity was comparable to the activated forms of YAP and TAZ, YAP5SA and TAZ4SA, in which the LATS kinase phosphorylation sites are mutated rendering them constitutively active (Zhao et al., 2010; Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 1C) and citation to prior work on YAP5SA and TAZ4SA (Zhao et al., 2010).

claim: Ectopic expression of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 in HEK293T cells promotes cell proliferation.
source: we showed that ectopic expression of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 in HEK293T cells promotes cell proliferation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: Demonstrated by EdU staining showing increased percentage of EdU-positive cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: The ability of VGLL2-NCOA2 to induce downstream transcription requires both its N-terminal VGLL2 and C-terminal NCOA2 fusion parts.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrated that the ability of VGLL2-NCOA2 to induce downstream transcription requires both its N-terminal VGLL2 and C-terminal NCOA2 fusion parts
evidence: Demonstrated by deletion constructs showing loss of activity when either part is deleted (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).

claim: The transcriptional effect of VGLL2-NCOA2 is dose-dependent.
source: this effect is dose-dependent and not affected by the 5′ or 3′ protein tags (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–H).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assays with increasing amounts of VGLL2-NCOA2 expression construct (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-F).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 strongly induce the expression of bona fide TEAD downstream target genes CCN2, CCN1, ANKRD1, and AMOTL2.
source: similar to activated YAP, the VGLL2-NCOA2, and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins also strongly induced the expression of bona fide TEAD downstream target genes, such as CCN2 (CTGF), CCN1 (CYR61), ANKRD1, and AMOTL2 (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by RNA-seq heatmap (Figure 1D) and RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 1E).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 is strongly associated with TEAD1 but not YAP5SA.
source: We performed co-IP assays in HEK293T cells expressing VGLL2-NCOA2, YAP5SA, and TEAD1 and demonstrated that VGLL2-NCOA2 was strongly associated with TEAD1 but not YAP5SA (Figure 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation assays (Figure 2A).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 can bind to endogenous TEAD proteins.
source: Furthermore, we showed that VGLL2-NCOA2 could bind to the endogenous TEAD proteins
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays detecting endogenous TEAD (Figure 2B).

claim: Strong interaction between VGLL2-NCOA2 and endogenous YAP and TAZ proteins in HEK293T cells was not detected.
source: however, we did not detect a strong interaction between VGLL2-NCOA2 and endogenous YAP and TAZ proteins in HEK293T cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays (Figure 2B).

claim: TEAD1 is able to bind YAP/TAZ.
source: Not surprisingly, TEAD1 was able to bind YAP/TAZ
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays (Figure 2C) and draws on established knowledge of TEAD-YAP/TAZ interaction.

claim: The interaction between TEAD1-NCOA2 and endogenous YAP/TAZ was not detected.
source: however, the interaction between TEAD1-NCOA2 and endogenous YAP/TAZ was not detected (Figure 2C)
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays (Figure 2C).

claim: CP1 effectively inhibits YAP5SA- and VGLL2-NCOA2-induced transcriptional activation.
source: Upon treatment with the TEAD palmitoylation inhibitor CP1 in HEK293T cells transfected with YAP5SA, VGLL2-NCOA2, and TEAD1-NCOA2, we found that CP1 effectively inhibited YAP5SA- and VGLL2-NCOA2-induced transcriptional activation
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 2D).

claim: CP1 has largely no effect on TEAD1-NCOA2-induced reporter activation.
source: but had largely no effect on TEAD1-NCOA2-induced reporter activation (Figure 2D).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 2D).

claim: The inability of CP1 to inhibit TEAD1-NCOA2 activity is likely because the TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion does not contain the auto-palmitoylation sites in the C-terminal YAP-binding domain of TEAD1.
source: The inability of CP1 to inhibit TEAD1-NCOA2 activity is likely because the TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion does not contain the auto-palmitoylation sites in the C-terminal YAP-binding domain of TEAD1.
evidence: Based on the protein structure (Figure 1A) and the known mechanism of CP1 targeting TEAD auto-palmitoylation (Li et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2022).

claim: TEAD-ENR potently inhibits the transcriptional activation of YAP5SA, VGLL2-NCOA2, and TEAD1-NCOA2.
source: When co-expressed with YAP5SA, VGLL2-NCOA2, and TEAD1-NCOA2 in HEK293T cells, TEAD-ENR potently inhibited the transcriptional activation of all three proteins (Figure 2D).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 2D).

claim: Downstream TEAD activity and TEAD DNA binding are critical for both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins.
source: These results from both the TEAD inhibitor and transcriptional repressor suggest that downstream TEAD activity and TEAD DNA binding are critical for both fusion proteins.
evidence: Based on the results from CP1 treatment and TEAD-ENR co-expression experiments (Figure 2D).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 can bind to endogenous TEAD proteins at similar levels in both control and YAP/TAZ-knockdown HEK293T cells.
source: We showed that VGLL2-NCOA2 could bind to endogenous TEAD proteins at similar levels in both control and YAP/TAZ-knockdown HEK293T cells (Figure 2G)
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays in cells with YAP/TAZ knockdown (Figure 2G).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 association with TEADs does not require YAP/TAZ.
source: suggesting its association with TEADs does not require YAP/TAZ.
evidence: Based on co-IP results showing maintained TEAD binding in YAP/TAZ knockdown cells (Figure 2G).

claim: Both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 robustly induce the transcription of CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1 in HEK293T cells with YAP/TAZ knockdown.
source: Furthermore, we found that both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 still robustly induced the transcription of the known TEAD target genes, including CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1, in HEK293T cells with YAP/TAZ knockdown (Figure 2H).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR analysis in YAP/TAZ knockdown cells (Figure 2H).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-induced transcriptional activation requires TEAD DNA binding but is YAP/TAZ independent.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-induced transcriptional activation requires TEAD DNA binding but is YAP/TAZ independent.
evidence: Based on the combined results from TEAD inhibitor/repressor experiments and YAP/TAZ knockdown experiments (Figures 2D, 2G, 2H).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP control overlapping yet distinct chromatin landscapes and downstream transcriptional programs.
source: we determined that VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP controlled overlapping yet distinct chromatin landscapes and downstream transcriptional programs (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, and RNA-seq analyses (Figure 3).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP5SA likely drive open chromatin architecture in a shared set of genes.
source: the analysis of differentially accessible chromatin sites annotated to the nearest genes showed significant enrichment of Hippo pathway-related genes in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP5SA-expressing cells (Figure 3A–C), suggesting that VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP5SA likely drive open chromatin architecture in a shared set of genes.
evidence: Based on ATAC-seq analysis showing enrichment of Hippo pathway genes (Figure 3A-C).

claim: Both VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP prefer to occupy distal genomic regions that are not in close proximity to the TSS (0–2 kb).
source: Annotation of CUT&RUN peaks with respect to their nearest gene transcriptional start site (TSS) showed that both VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP preferred to occupy distal genomic regions that are not in close proximity to the TSS (0–2 kb) (Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by CUT&RUN peak annotation analysis (Figure 3D).

claim: YAP preferentially binds to distal enhancer regions.
source: This is consistent with prior reports that YAP preferentially binds to distal enhancer regions (Zanconato et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2016)
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Zanconato et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2016).

claim: The VGLL2-NCOA2 fusion protein regulates downstream gene transcription through active enhancers.
source: and indicates that the VGLL2-NCOA2 fusion protein also regulates downstream gene transcription through active enhancers.
evidence: Based on CUT&RUN peak distribution showing distal binding (Figure 3D) and comparison to known YAP behavior.

claim: The TEAD binding sequence is among the most enriched motifs in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP5SA CUT&RUN peaks.
source: de novo motif analysis of our CUT&RUN datasets revealed that the TEAD binding sequence was among the most enriched motifs in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP5SA CUT&RUN peaks (Figure 3E)
evidence: Demonstrated by motif enrichment analysis of CUT&RUN data (Figure 3E).

claim: The AP1 motif is enriched in VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN peaks.
source: Interestingly, the AP1 motif was also enriched in VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN peaks (Figure 3E)
evidence: Demonstrated by motif enrichment analysis (Figure 3E).

claim: AP1 has proposed roles in TEAD-mediated transcription.
source: highlighting its proposed roles in TEAD-mediated transcription (Zanconato et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Zanconato et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2016).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP occupy the same genomic regions in the loci of CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1.
source: Furthermore, we compared the binding profiles of the bona fide downstream target genes of VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP identified in our CUT&RUN analysis, CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1, and showed that VGLL2-NCOA2 and YAP occupied the same genomic regions in the loci of the three genes (Figure 3F).
evidence: Demonstrated by CUT&RUN genomic tracks (Figure 3F).

claim: CREBBP and EP300 were among the hits specifically associated with VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 in the BioID assays.
source: Focusing on epigenetic and transcriptional regulators identified in the screens, we found that CREBBP (CBP) and EP300 (P300) were among the hits specifically associated with VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 in the BioID assays (Figure 4A).
evidence: Demonstrated by BioID proteomics screens (Figure 4A).

claim: TEAD proteins were among the few proteins associated with all four proteins (YAP5SA, TAZ4SA, VGLL2-NCOA2, and TEAD1-NCOA2) in BioID assays.
source: By intersecting the hits associated with YAP/TAZ or VGLL2-NCOA2/TEAD1-NCOA2, we found that TEAD proteins were among the few proteins associated with all four proteins, providing validation of our BioID datasets (Figure 4A).
evidence: Demonstrated by BioID proteomics screens (Figure 4A).

claim: CREBBP and EP300 are closely related histone acetyltransferases known for their function to induce histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) at the promoter and enhancer regions, thereby activating gene transcription.
source: The closely related histone acetyltransferases CREBBP and EP300, commonly referred to as CREBBP/EP300, are known for their function to induce histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) at the promoter and enhancer regions, thereby activating gene transcription (Ogryzko et al., 1996; Bannister and Kouzarides, 1996; Waddell et al., 2021; Hogg et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Ogryzko et al., 1996; Bannister and Kouzarides, 1996; Waddell et al., 2021; Hogg et al., 2021).

claim: CREBBP/EP300 has been reported to form a complex with the NCOA family proteins that play a critical role in the regulation of nuclear receptors-mediated transcription.
source: More importantly, CREBBP/EP300 has been reported to form a complex with the NCOA family proteins that play a critical role in the regulation of nuclear receptors-mediated transcription (Waddell et al., 2021; Yi et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Waddell et al., 2021; Yi et al., 2021).

claim: The C-terminal NCOA part of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusions interacts with CREBBP/EP300.
source: It is consistent with our proteomics data that the C-terminal NCOA part of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusions interacted with CREBBP/EP300 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Based on BioID proteomics data (Figure 4A) and confirmed by co-IP (Figure 5A).

claim: CREB motif is specifically enriched among VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN peaks, but not in YAP5SA peaks.
source: Interestingly, our motif enrichment analysis identified CREB motif as specifically enriched among VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN peaks, but not in YAP5SA peaks (Figure 3E).
evidence: Demonstrated by motif enrichment analysis (Figure 3E).

claim: CREB is a known transcription factor interacting with CREBBP/EP300.
source: CREB is a known transcription factor interacting with CREBBP/EP300 (Chrivia et al., 1993)
evidence: Cited from prior publication (Chrivia et al., 1993).

claim: The activity of CREBBP/EP300 has been implicated in several types of human cancers.
source: In addition, the activity of CREBBP/EP300 has been implicated in several types of human cancers (Waddell et al., 2021; Hogg et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Waddell et al., 2021; Hogg et al., 2021).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2, but not YAP5SA, are strongly associated with endogenous EP300 proteins.
source: We performed the co-IP analysis in HEK293T cells overexpressing VGLL2-NCOA2, TEAD1-NCOA2, and YAP5SA and demonstrated that VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2, but not YAP5SA, were strongly associated with endogenous EP300 proteins (Figure 4B)
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays (Figure 4B).

claim: EP300 binding peaks show significant enrichment of Hippo pathway-related genes in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 expressing cells but not in the control cells.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis of EP300 binding peaks annotated by the nearest genes showed significant enrichment of Hippo pathway-related genes in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 expressing cells but not in the control cells (Figure 4C)
evidence: Demonstrated by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis of EP300 CUT&RUN peaks (Figure 4C).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins recruit the CREBBP/EP300 complex to a specific set of genes, likely including the TEAD-dependent downstream target genes.
source: suggesting that VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins recruit the CREBBP/EP300 complex to a specific set of genes, likely including the TEAD-dependent downstream target genes.
evidence: Based on EP300 CUT&RUN showing enrichment at Hippo pathway genes (Figure 4C) and motif analysis showing TEAD motifs (Figure 4D).

claim: TEAD and AP1 binding sequences are among the top-ranking motifs identified in EP300 occupied genomic sites, specifically in VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells.
source: In keeping with this result, our de novo motif analysis also revealed that TEAD and AP1 binding sequences were among the top-ranking motifs identified in EP300 occupied genomic sites, specifically in VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: Demonstrated by motif enrichment analysis of EP300 CUT&RUN peaks (Figure 4D).

claim: The CREB binding sequence is one of the top-ranking motifs identified in EP300 peaks in both control and VGLL2-NCOA2/TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells.
source: Interestingly, we noticed that the CREB binding sequence was one of the top-ranking motifs identified in EP300 peaks in both control and VGLL2-NCOA2/TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells (Figure 4D)
evidence: Demonstrated by motif enrichment analysis (Figure 4D).

claim: EP300 binds to the loci of CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1 in VGLL2-NCOA2/TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells, but not in control cells.
source: Upon further examining the binding profiles of EP300 in the loci of CCN1, CCN2, and ANKRD1, we showed that EP300 bound to these loci in VGLL2-NCOA2/TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing cells, but not in control cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: Demonstrated by EP300 CUT&RUN genomic tracks (Figure 4E).

claim: EP300 binds to the same genomic regions that are also occupied by VGLL2-NCOA2.
source: More importantly, EP300 bound to the same genomic regions that were also occupied by VGLL2-NCOA2 identified in VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN assay (Figure 3F).
evidence: Based on comparison of EP300 CUT&RUN (Figure 4E) and VGLL2-NCOA2 CUT&RUN (Figure 3F) genomic tracks.

claim: EP300 occupies genomic sites within the CREB3 locus in cells with or without the expression of the fusion proteins.
source: As a control, we showed that EP300 occupied the genomic sites within the CREB3 locus in cells with or without the expression of the fusion proteins (Figure 4E).
evidence: Demonstrated by EP300 CUT&RUN genomic tracks (Figure 4E).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins interact with CREBBP/EP300, recruiting them to promote TEAD target gene expression.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins interact with CREBBP/EP300, recruiting them to promote TEAD target gene expression.
evidence: Based on combined results from BioID, co-IP, and CUT&RUN experiments (Figures 4A-E).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 can induce oncogenic transformation of C2C12 cells in cell culture and allograft mouse tumor models.
source: Prior reports have demonstrated that VGLL2-NCOA2 can induce oncogenic transformation of C2C12 cells in cell culture and allograft mouse tumor models (Watson et al., 2023).
evidence: Cited from prior publication (Watson et al., 2023).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 binds to EP300 via its C-terminal NCOA2 part.
source: We first demonstrated that VGLL2-NCOA2 binds to EP300 via its C-terminal NCOA2 part using co-immunoprecipitation assays (Figure 5A)
evidence: Demonstrated by co-IP assays with deletion constructs (Figure 5A).

claim: The NCOA2 part of the fusion proteins is essential for recruiting EP300 to induce downstream transcription and tumorigenesis.
source: highlighting the essential role of the NCOA2 part of the fusion proteins in recruiting EP300 to induce downstream transcription and tumorigenesis.
evidence: Based on co-IP results showing NCOA2 is required for EP300 binding (Figure 5A).

claim: Expression of both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins is able to robustly induce the transcription of Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1 in C2C12 cells.
source: We found that the expression of both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins was able to robustly induce the transcription of the known Tead target genes, Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1, in C2C12 cells (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR analysis in C2C12 cells (Figure 5B-D).

claim: EP300 inhibition by A485 treatment strongly inhibits transcriptional upregulation of Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1 induced by the fusion proteins.
source: By utilizing a potent EP300 small-molecule inhibitor, A485, which inhibits CREBBP/EP300 activity both in vitro and in vivo (Hogg et al., 2021; Lasko et al., 2017), we showed that EP300 inhibition by A485 treatment strongly inhibited transcriptional upregulation of Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1 induced by the fusion proteins (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR analysis with A485 treatment (Figure 5B-D) and cites prior work on A485 (Hogg et al., 2021; Lasko et al., 2017).

claim: A485 is not able to strongly block YAP5SA-induced Tead target gene expression in C2C12 cells.
source: In contrast, A485 was not able to strongly block YAP5SA-induced Tead target gene expression in C2C12 cells (Figure 5B–D)
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR analysis with A485 treatment (Figure 5B-D).

claim: CREBBP/EP300 is required for VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2-dependent gene expression but is largely dispensable for YAP/TAZ-induced target gene transcription.
source: suggesting that CREBBP/EP300 is required for VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2-dependent gene expression but is largely dispensable for YAP/TAZ-induced target gene transcription.
evidence: Based on differential effects of A485 on fusion proteins versus YAP5SA (Figure 5B-D).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 are able to induce colony formation of C2C12 cells in soft agar.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrated that VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 were also able to induce colony formation of C2C12 cells in soft agar (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated by soft agar colony formation assays (Figure 5E).

claim: A485 treatment markedly reduces the numbers and sizes of the soft agar colonies induced by TEAD1-NCOA2 and VGLL2-NCOA2 but not YAP5SA.
source: More importantly, A485 treatment markedly reduced the numbers and sizes of the soft agar colonies induced by TEAD1-NCOA2 and VGLL2-NCOA2 but not YAP5SA (Figure 5F and G)
evidence: Demonstrated by soft agar colony formation assays with A485 treatment (Figure 5F and G).

claim: Both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing C2C12 cells are able to generate aggressive tumors when allografted into nude mice.
source: we took advantage of the C2C12 allograft tumor models and demonstrated that both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing C2C12 cells were able to generate aggressive tumors when allografted into nude mice, leading to termination of tumor-bearing mice at around 30 days post-injection.
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo allograft experiments (Figure 6).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing tumors are highly proliferative, measured by Ki67 staining.
source: These VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing tumors were highly proliferative, measured by Ki67 staining
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining (Figure 6A).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2- and TEAD1-NCOA2-expressing tumors exhibit heterogeneous expression of Desmin.
source: but exhibited heterogeneous expression of Desmin (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining (Figure 6A).

claim: EP300 inhibition by A485 significantly blocks tumor growth in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 allograft tumor models.
source: In addition, we found that EP300 inhibition by A485 significantly blocked the tumor growth in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 allograft tumor models (Figure 6C and D)
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor volume measurements in A485-treated mice (Figure 6C and D).

claim: A485 treatment markedly decreases the proliferation of tumor cells in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 tumor models.
source: and A485 treatment markedly decreased the proliferation of tumor cells (Figure 6E and F)
evidence: Demonstrated by Ki67 IHC staining (Figure 6E and F).

claim: A485 treatment decreases the transcription of Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1 in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 tumor models.
source: and the transcription of the target genes, including Ccn1, Ccn2, and Ankrd1 (Figure 6G and H), in both VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 tumor models.
evidence: Demonstrated by RT-qPCR analysis of tumor tissue (Figure 6G and H).

claim: The CREBBP/EP300 factors are essential for tumorigenesis induced by VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins.
source: Together, these data, both in vitro and in vivo, suggest that the CREBBP/EP300 factors are essential for tumorigenesis induced by VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins.
evidence: Based on combined in vitro and in vivo results showing A485 inhibits fusion protein-driven transformation (Figures 5 and 6).

claim: Misregulation of YAP and TAZ, including protein upregulation, nuclear accumulation, and fusion translocation, has emerged as a major mechanism underlying Hippo signaling involvement in tumorigenesis.
source: Misregulation of YAP and TAZ, including protein upregulation, nuclear accumulation, and fusion translocation, has emerged as a major mechanism underlying Hippo signaling involvement in tumorigenesis (Piccolo et al., 2023; Thompson, 2020; Franklin et al., 2023; Szulzewsky et al., 2021; Garcia et al., 2022).
evidence: Cited from prior publications (Piccolo et al., 2023; Thompson, 2020; Franklin et al., 2023; Szulzewsky et al., 2021; Garcia et al., 2022).

claim: VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins provide a distinct mechanism of oncogenic transformation that is related to the Hippo pathway but independent of the YAP/TAZ function.
source: In this work, our characterization of VGLL2-NCOA2 and TEAD1-NCOA2 fusion proteins generated by recurrent rearrangement in scRMS provides a distinct mechanism of oncogenic transformation that is related to the Hippo pathway but independent of the YAP/TAZ function.
evidence: Based on the combined results from the study showing YAP/TAZ-independent TEAD activation.

claim: VGLL4 is a bona fide transcriptional repressor for YAP/TAZ via its two TEAD-binding TDU domain.
source: Among the members of the VGLL family proteins, VGLL4 stands out as a bona fide transcriptional repressor for YAP/TAZ via its two TEAD-binding TDU domain.
evidence: Draws on established knowledge from prior work on VGLL4 (Koontz et al., 2013; Cai et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2014; Li et al., 2023).

claim: VGLL1-3 contain a single TDU domain.
source: The other members of the family, VGLL1-3, contain a single TDU domain
evidence: Based on protein structure knowledge and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: VGLL2 itself does not appear to be a strong activator of TEAD-mediated transcription, even when overexpressed in cells.
